801-about-the-trottier-institute-for-sus: Founded in 2012 with a Trottier Family Foundation gift: research, courses and public education on sustainability. Offers a non-thesis M.Eng. for those with engineering, planning or architecture degrees, including industrial ecology and life-cycle assessment.
801-undergraduate-courses-at-tised: These TISED courses are open to undergraduates.
801-location: Lorne M. Trottier Building, Room 2054, 3630 University St.
801-about-the-school-of-urban-planning: How communities shape their environments, a profession about a century old, tackling social, economic and environmental resilience and justice through multidisciplinary, collaborative work. Graduate only: accredited M.U.P., thesis M.Sc., and Ph.D.
802-location: Macdonald-Harrington Building, Room 400, 815 Sherbrooke St. W.
802-about-the-department-of-bioresource-: Agricultural and Environmental Sciences offers accredited B.Eng. programs, with Honours and Professional Agrology options, at Macdonald, 35 km from downtown. BREE courses may interest other engineers. See p. 100.
803-minor-programs-in-the-faculty-of-eng: 18–24 credits, overlapping 6–12 with your degree, so typically one extra term. C or better throughout. See your department about complementaries.
Arts minor concentrations are possible through the Minor Webform, up to 9 overlapping credits.
803-available-programs: For others, ask an adviser at MESC.
803-computer-science-courses-and-minor-p: Many COMP courses for engineers, including COMP 208 in most B.Eng. programs. The Minor needs 24 credits with C or better. Contact the Undergraduate Program Coordinator, McConnell, Room 320.
803-minor-in-environment: Why environmental problems are complex and contested, from Bieler. 18 credits beyond the B.Eng., approved by your adviser and the Minor's (p. 823).
804-minor-program-in-management: See a MESC adviser before applying to Desautels. 18 credits from the core, not those overlapping Engineering, with extra credits needed. Up to 6 Group B credits may count for both. Admission rules change yearly. Courses needing statistics require MGCR 271 or equivalent.
804-application-and-program-requirements: See Desautels' Minor page and the Faculty's site.
804-minor-in-musical-science-and-technol: Science and technology applied to music. Apply online by the deadline. See Schulich's site.
804-program-description: Aircraft and spacecraft design, with streams in aerodynamics and propulsion, structures, materials, spacecraft and avionics. At most 9 credits shared with the major.
804-complementary-courses-12-credits: From one stream; one course outside it with the Adviser's approval first.
805-program-description: For all engineering students: AI techniques for your field. Seven courses, up to three shared with the major.
805-group-a: 3 credits. COMP 250 and ECSE 250 can't both be taken.
805-group-b: 4 credits. Not both ECSE 551 and COMP 551.
806-group-e: 9–12 credits, or 400–500 AI topics courses with ECE's approval. Not both COMP 424 and ECSE 526, or ECSE 507 and MECH 579.
806-program-description: For B.Eng. and B.Sc.(Arch.): 24 credits chosen with the Faculty Student Adviser, Adams Room 22. C or better.
806-requirements: At least two Arts areas with 6+ in each, and 12 at 300+. At most 9 from your Complementary Studies.
806-program-description-2: Engineering applied to medicine: life sciences, plus areas like artificial organs, bioinformatics, biomaterials, biomechanics, imaging and neural systems. For Engineering and Bioresource students, C or better, with as few as 9 extra credits and up to 12 overlapping. Advisers: Prof. R. Leask, Prof. R. Mongrain, Prof. G. Mitsis.
807-introductory-life-sciences: At least 3 credits, with one each from the overlapping molecular and cell biology sets. One isn't for Chemical Engineering students.
807-specialization-courses: At least 12, with 6 outside your department and one BMDE, best taken late.
808-neural-systems-and-biosignal-process: BIEN 350 or ECSE 206. 0–6 more by permission.
808-program-description: Designed for Chemical Engineering, open to others. 24 credits, 18 exclusive to it, substituting any already in your major. Chemical Engineers can use BIOT 505 as a complementary, adding 15 credits. Advisers: MESC, and Nancy Nelson for Science.
809-alternative-required-courses-for-che: These courses plus one complementary, not FACC 300.
809-complementary-courses: 12 credits outside your department or from the lists, at least three in one area.
809-management: Can't count toward a Management minor or Complementary Studies.
809-pollution: Can't count toward the Environmental Engineering Minor.
810-program-description: Adviser: Dr. Samuel Sewall. C or better.
810-complementary-courses: 15 credits, two with labs. CHEM 212 is needed for most; CHEM 213 and 273 for physical chemistry. CHEM 222 instead of 234 counts as one lab, but you still need 25 credits.
810-program-description-2: 24–26 credits of core concepts, for B.Eng. and B.Sc.(Arch.) students with ECSE 202, COMP 202 or 208, not Software Co-op. C or better, at most 6 overlapping. See the Coordinator, Adviser and your department. Forms by the end of add/drop in your final term.
811-complementary-courses-21-23-credits: 3, 3, 3–4 and 3–4 from four lists, and 9 at COMP 300+ (not 396 or 400). COMP 251 is strongly recommended.
811-program-description: Project management, construction law, labour relations, accounting and finance, and related fields. For Civil mainly, open to all B.Eng. and B.Sc.(Arch.). C or better, up to 12 overlapping.
812-list-b: One course is in French at Polytechnique.
812-program-description: What societies produce, prices, rates and inflation, consumers, and policy. At most 9 overlapping.
812-required-courses-18-credits: 6 and 12 from the lists. ECON 209, or 332 and 333. One is only for Mining and Materials students.
812-program-description-2: Environmental engineering principles, by Civil, for all Engineering and Bioresource students. Not all courses run yearly. Up to 12 overlapping.
813-stream-a: 15 from Engineering and 3 from Non-Engineering, at least 6 outside your department, up to 6 of environmental research projects with approval.
813-stream-b: 9 from the BITS field semester, approved by the Coordinator, and 9 from Engineering, not CHEE 496.
813-engineering-course-list: At Macdonald and downtown. BREE 217 and CIVE 323 exclude each other.
813-non-engineering-course-list: At Macdonald and downtown. One excludes those with CHEE 370.
814-program-description: 24 credits, as few as 15 extra. Coordinator: Prof. Richard Chromik, Wong 2620.
814-program-description-2: A stronger math base for all Engineering students, including Architecture, chosen with advisers from U2. At most 9 overlapping. C or better.
815-complementary-courses-15-credits: 3 from the first list, 6–12 from the second, 0–6 approved. After ECSE 205, no MATH 323 or 324. MATH 271 or 319. MATH 262, 263 and 338 don't count.
815-program-description: 23–25 credits on exploration, extraction and processing, with an industrial work term, possibly limited.
816-program-description: 21–22 credits from Science, Engineering and Medicine on making, studying and using nanomaterials in medicine, electronics and energy, and their impacts. Year 2 or higher, up to 12 overlapping. Check prerequisites.
816-group-a: At least 3. One each from the listed sets. Some need CGPA 3.0.
817-group-b: 18–19, depending on Group A. A nanotechnology research course, up to 4 credits, may count with prior approval.
817-chemical-engineering: One each from the listed sets.
817-electrical-engineering: Some need CGPA 3.0. One each from the listed sets.
817-mechanical-engineering: With the Adviser's approval when the topic fits. One each from the listed sets.
818-program-description: Thermal and quantum physics, for Honours Electrical and Mechanical students, with authorization. At most 9 overlapping.
819-program-description: Basic computer science, programming and software practice, with no professional recognition. Six courses, 18 credits, two shared.
819-complementary-courses: 3 and 6 from two lists. Only one each of COMP 250 or ECSE 250, COMP 424 or ECSE 526, ECSE 439 or 539, ECSE 446 or 546. Some need Honours, or CGPA 3.0 with B+ in prerequisites.
819-program-description-2: With Desautels: seeing opportunity and acting on it, across ventures, social enterprise, start-ups, co-ops, corporate ventures and side projects. Up to 6 of Group B or electives can overlap.
